clue.text: Tense choir sit nervously here

indicators.note: something done nervously is jittery and disordered, so the letters of choir and sit are jumbled

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A choir sits jittery and tense, waiting to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervously' rearranges CHOIRSIT into HISTORIC; 'Tense' looks like an adjective for the nervous choir but is the grammatical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic present is a verb tense: narrating past events with present forms for vividness.

clue.text: Leave short gardening tool on stone

indicators.note: short asks for the word for the tool to lose its final letter

parts.note: a hoe is a gardening tool for weeding
a pit is the stone of a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone sets a stubby hoe down on a stone in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like a noun or a polite request; it is a blunt British order to go away. In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A brusque British imperative telling someone to go away, an order to depart.

clue.text: Captain's right having most important player on committee

parts.note: the star is a team's leading player
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A team captain's privilege is to have the star player on the selection committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captain's right' suggests an entitlement; it is the ship's right-hand side as a captain would name it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term for the right-hand side of a vessel facing forward, as used aboard ship.

clue.text: Poet going west in Vladivostok

indicators.note: in an across clue's direction west is leftwards, so the run of letters is read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the word Vladivostok

explanation.surface: A poet heads west while staying in Vladivostok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to DIVO inside vlaDIVOstok, and 'going west' turns it right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Publius Ovidius Naso, the Roman author of the Metamorphoses, a classical versifier.

clue.text: Disinclination to act in the queen with headdress only 60% complete

parts.note: taken as written
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the queen

indicators.note: sixty per cent of a five-letter word keeps its first three letters and drops the rest

parts.note: a tiara is a jewelled headdress

explanation.surface: A queen too lazy to finish putting on her headdress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only 60% complete' cuts TIARA to TIA, its first three of five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggishness, a tendency to stay inactive rather than move.

clue.text: Part of 14 having little volume during game

indicators.note: during says the small measure comes in the middle of the sport

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
1 cc, one cubic centimetre, is a tiny volume, with I as the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A small, quiet instrument heard in the middle of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little volume' tempts as quietness; it is one cubic centimetre, written I CC. 14 is ORCHESTRA, and this small flute is part of its woodwind.
explanation.definitionFit: A small high-pitched flute, one of the woodwind instruments of an orchestra.

clue.text: Tackle guys on crack in heart of ghetto

indicators.note: in places the joke and the men between the central letters of ghetto
the heart of a word is its middle, here the two central letters of ghetto
on links the men to the crack, the two pieces joined in sequence

parts.note: a crack is a wisecrack, a quip
guys means men

explanation.surface: Gang members go on crack cocaine in the middle of the ghetto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes the middle two letters of ghetto, which split to hold the rest. 'crack' is a joke, not a drug, and 'Tackle' is gear rather than a challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle means gear or apparatus, as in fishing tackle, the kit needed for a task.

clue.text: It normally takes two or three shots to shoot this flier

definitions.text: It normally takes two or three shots to shoot this
definitions.meaning: in golf, a score of two under par on a hole, usually two strokes on a par four or three on a par five

explanation.surface: A hunter usually needs several shots to bring down a big bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hunter; 'shoot' is the golfer's word for scoring. 'normally' allows for the rare hole in one on a par three.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: golf's score of two under par on a hole, and a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Distressed chaps stuffing cake at start of diet

indicators.note: stuffing puts the chaps inside the cake as a filling

parts.note: a torte is a rich layered cake
chaps means men

indicators.note: the start of diet is its first letter

explanation.surface: Men upset at gorging on cake just as their diet begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffing' suggests overeating but puts one piece inside the other; 'at start of' adds the first letter of diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tormented means anguished or suffering, deeply troubled in mind.

clue.text: Sweet pair starting a row

indicators.note: starting says the pair comes at the beginning, ahead of the rest

parts.note: a line is a row

explanation.surface: A couple of sweethearts begin an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel; it is a line in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A confection of nuts in caramelised sugar, a type of confectionery.

clue.text: With good cause, annoying high street solicitor

definitions.text: With good cause, annoying high street solicitor

parts.words: With good cause, annoying high street solicitor
parts.note: reads like a justified lawyer on the main street, but the solicitor accosts shoppers to sign up donations for a charity, a portmanteau of charity and mugger

explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a British lawyer with a high street office; here it is one who solicits, and 'good cause' means a charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a street fundraiser who pesters passers-by for regular donations.

clue.text: Objection about a part of 14?

indicators.note: about turns the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a section of the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses BUT to TUB; 14 is ORCHESTRA, and this brass instrument is one of its members.
explanation.definitionFit: A large low-pitched brass instrument, a member of an orchestra's brass section.

clue.text: Tatty rest-home with a quiet ambience

indicators.note: tatty means shabby and in disrepair, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quiet

explanation.surface: A shabby care home with a peaceful feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tatty' rearranges RESTHOME, A and P (quiet).
explanation.definitionFit: Ambience is a place's mood or feel, its prevailing air.

clue.text: Melody maker put pressure on man city about leader of oasis

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: about says the man and city go around the letter taken from oasis

parts.note: Ian is a man's name
LA is Los Angeles, a city

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Manchester City fans pressure the Oasis frontman, a Man City supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man city' looks like Manchester City (the Oasis band's Gallagher brothers are fans), but splits into a man's name and a city around the first letter of oasis.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-playing mechanical keyboard that produces tunes from a perforated roll.

clue.text: Exotic myrrh put round Egyptian flower

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the Egyptian's letter
exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is an abbreviation of Egyptian, as in the Egyptian pound

explanation.surface: Fragrant resin is placed around an Egyptian flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic' rearranges MYRRHPUT into PYRTHRUM, and 'round' puts it around E.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like chrysanthemum species, a garden plant also used for insecticide.

clue.text: Actor starts to recite Hamlet's speech — exciting poor folk in the pit

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters are reworked
the starts of the four words are their first letters

explanation.surface: An actor begins reciting Hamlet's speech but performs it poorly before the audience in the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes RHSE from recite, Hamlet's, speech, exciting; 'poor' rearranges these with ACTOR. The pit is the sunken area for musicians, not the groundlings.
explanation.definitionFit: Instrumental musicians playing in the sunken area before a theatre stage.

clue.text: Works with preservationists producing effects

parts.note: opera is the plural of opus, a work
NT is the National Trust, the British body that preserves historic buildings and land

explanation.surface: Conservation volunteers doing practical work.
explanation.walkthrough: OPERA here is the plural of opus; the National Trust is a British heritage charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Operant means active or effective, having an influence on results.

clue.text: A good deal is required to get this bid in solo whist

definitions.text: A good deal is required to get this bid in solo whist

parts.words: A good deal is required to get this bid in solo whist
parts.note: reads as needing a strong hand of cards, while the call itself means plenty: in solo whist it promises nine of the thirteen tricks

explanation.surface: Only a strong hand of cards justifies this ambitious call at the whist table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' is both the cards dealt and a large amount, which is the word's plain sense. Solo whist is a British trick-taking card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A plentiful amount, and in solo whist a high bid to take nine tricks.

clue.text: One making weaker solution for photographer

definitions.meaning: a chemical bath used in developing to thin the density of a negative

explanation.walkthrough: 'solution' suggests an answer to a problem; it is a liquid chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: something that lessens, and a darkroom chemical that thins a dense negative.

clue.text: Shankar takes pressed oil for a dish in the trattoria

parts.note: Ravi Shankar was the Indian sitar virtuoso

indicators.note: pressed means squeezed out of shape, so the letters of oil are reordered

explanation.surface: The sitar player orders a dish cooked in pressed olive oil at an Italian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressed' looks like describing the oil but rearranges OIL into OLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pasta parcels with a filling, an Italian restaurant dish.

clue.text: Bowl over American tenor captivated by upright

indicators.note: captivated by means held inside, so the tenor sits within the upright word

parts.note: upright means honest, morally sound

explanation.surface: An American tenor charmed by an upright piano would be bowled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upright' tempts as the piano; it is sound in the moral sense, with T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl over is to amaze, to stun with surprise.

clue.text: A chair is broken by Conservative, being very old

indicators.note: a chair that is broken falls apart, so its letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician breaks an ancient chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is broken' rearranges the letters of 'A chair'; the C for Conservative then follows rather than going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means antiquated, belonging to a much earlier period.

clue.text: Cod put on last scrap of newspaper — a substitute for china

parts.note: cod as a verb means to hoax or tease

indicators.note: the last scrap of a word is its final letter

parts.note: vice means in place of, as in vice-captain, standing in for another

explanation.surface: Fish wrapped in the last bit of newspaper as stand-in for a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cod' is not fish but a verb, to kid; VICE is a substitute, as in vice-president. China here is crockery, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching set of cups, saucers and pot made of porcelain.

clue.text: Champion jockey caught leaving crime

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for caught departs from the jockey's name

parts.note: Willie Carson was five times British champion flat-racing jockey
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A champion jockey is caught out leaving the scene of a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Willie Carson was a famous British jockey; 'leaving' removes the C for caught.
explanation.definitionFit: The crime of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: English crackers passed round as accompaniment to this?

definitions.text: English crackers passed round as accompaniment to this?

indicators.note: passed round means turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: crackers means mad

explanation.surface: English crackers handed round to go with the cheese board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits but means mad, reversed after E; the whole clue then describes a cheese eaten with crackers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild Dutch cheese in a red wax coat, often served with biscuits.

clue.text: Joint finally lit in bog

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for bog

parts.note: a mire is a bog

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter

explanation.surface: Smoking a spliff, finally lit, out in the marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a cannabis cigarette; it is a carpentry joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworking joint where two pieces meet at an angle, as in a picture frame corner.

clue.text: Research establishment erected on one island

indicators.note: erected means put upright, which in a down clue turns the word to read upwards

parts.note: a lab is a research laboratory
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A research lab is built on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' reverses LAB to BAL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indonesian island, a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: Is Roman emperor following right Italian course?

indicators.note: following says these pieces come after the right letter

parts.note: taken as written
Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Roman emperor did the right thing in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the other pieces after R. 'course' is a dish in a meal, not a direction; Otto was a name of four Holy Roman Emperors.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice dish cooked with stock, served as a course in an Italian meal.

clue.text: Not in favour of touching

definitions.meaning: in contact with, as a ladder leaning on a wall

explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' tempts as moving; it means in contact with.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: opposed to, and in physical contact with, as a bike leaning on a wall.

clue.text: Such languauge from drunk men in sedan chair!

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Drunken men in an imperial litter use coarse language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges MENINSEDANCHAIR; a mandarin was an imperial Chinese official carried in a sedan chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The standard spoken tongue of China, based on the Beijing dialect.
